You pursue growth relentlessly: holding a stable position is a slow loss, because the game is won only by taking 18 supply centers, and while you sit a rival grows. You form alliances when they advance you and honor them only while they pay, treating a quiet front as a chance to break rather than a comfort to keep. You read other powers from what they say and do, and you use deception and betrayal when the timing is right, while recognizing that careless, habitual betrayal makes you unpartnerable.

text: My core plan is to grab SER and RUM quickly while keeping Italy neutral or cooperative — I'll push A BUD to SER, A VIE to GAL or TRI depending on Russian and Italian intentions, and use F TRI to threaten ALB or ADR to set up a Balkan sweep. Within two turns I want SER, RUM, and GRE locked down to hit 6 supply centers, which means I need Russia distracted elsewhere and Italy either allied or blocked from TRI. I'll open diplomacy with Italy to propose a division of the Balkans and with Russia to gauge their intentions toward GAL and RUM.

England's classic opening is to seize Norway and position for Scandinavia while keeping France honest on the Channel. I'll move F EDI to NTH and F LON to ENG to dominate the northern seas and threaten both Norway and Belgium, while pushing A LVP to YOR as a flexible follow-up piece. Within two turns I want Norway and Belgium secured, giving me 5 centers and a strong platform to either press into Scandinavia or pivot against France depending on how negotiations develop.

}

Standard French opening: I'll take Iberia by moving F BRE to MAO (to convoy or escort into POR/SPA next) and A MAR to SPA for an early center, while A PAR goes to BUR to pressure Germany and keep Belgium in play. My aim is to hold Spain and Portugal by Fall, secure a Channel non-aggression pact with England, and use BUR as leverage toward Belgium against Germany.

I'll push F KIE to DEN to grab a northern supply center, move A BER to KIE to free up the Baltic approach, and send A MUN to BUR to contest the west and signal pressure on France while leaving options open for a deal. Within two turns I want DEN, HOL, and BEL secured to reach 6 centers, using England as a counterweight against France and Russia as a distraction for Austria. My opening diplomacy will propose a western split with England (I take DEN/HOL, they take NWY) and a non-aggression pact with France while I quietly position to stab if the opportunity arises.

I'll open with the classic Italian setup: F NAP to ION to threaten Tunis and eventually the eastern Mediterranean, A VEN to TYR to pressure Austria and position for a Lepanto or a western swing, and A ROM to APU to support a convoy into Tunis next fall. My two-turn goal is to take Tunis in Fall 1901 and secure a foothold in either Greece or the Balkans by 1902, while keeping Austria friendly enough to avoid a two-front war early on. I'll reach out to Austria about a non-aggression pact and probe Turkey's intentions, since the Lepanto (Italy-Austria vs. Turkey) is the most reliable path to eastern growth.

I'll push into the Balkans by moving A WAR to UKR and F SEV to RUM, aiming to secure Romania and Bulgaria within two turns while keeping F STP/SC ready to contest Scandinavia. I'll seek an early understanding with Austria to avoid a two-front war, and probe Turkey for a potential joint action against Austria if they're amenable.

Turkey's position is strong in the east but surrounded by potential threats. My immediate goal is to secure the Balkans (BUL, SER, GRE) and the eastern Mediterranean before Russia and Austria can consolidate there, while keeping my home centers defended. I'll advance CON toward BUL, push SMY toward ARM and SYR to claim eastern territory, and support these moves with ANK to establish a forward presence that makes me the dominant power in my region—this sets me up to either ally with a western power against the Balkans or pivot north into Russia's sphere if the opportunity arises.

I'll open diplomatic threads with Italy, Russia, and Turkey — the three powers most directly relevant to my Balkan ambitions. Italy needs to be kept neutral or cooperative regarding TRI. Russia needs to be gauged on GAL and RUM. Turkey is a potential rival in the Balkans but could also be steered toward conflict with Russia.
